tweets.text: 🇩🇪 Berlin found a use for its water cannons that doesn't involve a protest. As the city baked through record heat, police rolled two of them out in front of the Brandenburg Gate, the same vehicles normally used to break up crowds, and turned them on the public as a giant cooling mist. They worked their way through Potsdamer Platz, the Reichstag, and Mauerpark, going through some 9,000 liters in an afternoon. Germany had just hit 41.3 degrees, the hottest temperature it's ever recorded. The crowd, for once, cheered the water cannon. Writer: Julie Video

tweets.text: 🇨🇳 China's answer to a brutal heat wave: send out the water trucks. On the hottest days, sprinkler trucks hose down the roads so the water evaporates fast, pulling heat off the asphalt and cooling the air around it. It keeps the pavement from softening and takes the edge off the street-level swelter. They pull double duty too, knocking dust out of the air while they're at it. Writer: Julie Video
